title: Finance Note: Working Out the Benefit That Goes Across with a Transferred Piece
content:
**Scope.** This note works out the benefit that goes across with a piece when coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans passes to a new owner.

**1. The benefit standing on the plan.** The benefit standing on the plan is the allowance entries booked to it over the whole time it has been in force, less the benefit consumed. Where the benefit consumed comes to as much as those entries or more, the benefit standing is nothing rather than a negative amount.

**2. The benefit consumed.** The benefit consumed is the benefit taken by every settlement booked to the plan.

**3. How much carries across.** The new-plan share of the benefit standing carries across, being 70 percent of it.

**4. The claims answered on the plan.** What carries across is not reduced for the claims answered on the plan.

**5. Order and rounding.** The tenure share and the claims share both act on the benefit standing, one after the other, and what carries across is never below zero. The figure carried across is rounded to two decimal places once at the end.

## How periods are measured

The coverage year in progress runs from the anniversary of the day coverage began, and the months it has run so far are the whole months since coverage began beyond the coverage years already completed.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

The allowance entries booked to a plan over the whole time it has been in force come to 5000.00 USD, and the settlements booked to it have taken 1800.00 USD of benefit. The benefit standing on the plan is 3200.00 USD. The new-plan share of that standing benefit carries across, being 70 percent of 3200.00 USD, so 2240.00 USD is reached; what carries across is not reduced for the claims answered on the plan, so the figure stays there. Rounded to two decimal places once at the end, 2240.00 USD goes across with the piece.
